datasets.name: 96e65a6f
queryLines:
SELECT
    p.episode_id,
    a.day,
    a.phase,
    a.step_index,
    a.seat_index,
    p.player_id,
    p.model_name,
    p.role,
    p.team,
    a.action_type,
    a.target_id,
    a.message,
    a.reasoning,
    a.perceived_threat_level,
    CASE WHEN a.perceived_threat_level = 'SAFE' THEN 0
        WHEN a.perceived_threat_level = 'UNEASY' THEN 1
        ELSE 2
    END AS perceived_threat_level_int,
    a.prompt_tokens,
    a.completion_tokens,
    a.reported_cost
FROM silver.players p
INNER JOIN silver.actions a
ON p.episode_id = a.episode_id AND p.player_id = a.actor_id

lines: ## Kaggle LLM Werewolf Data Analysis *or, "Good call- you're absolutely right. I am a bloodthirsty night-beast, great catch!"* ### Overview - **Werewolf ** is (per Kaggle) "...a multiplayer social deduction game in which an informed minority (the werewolves) must deceive an uninformed majority (the villagers) to win." - Small number of werewolves collaborate to (\**ehem\**) "eliminate" villagers one-by-one, while attempting to avoid scrutiny and cast suspicion on other players - Villagers collaborate to identify and (\**ehem\**) "exile" the werewolves before the werewolves obtain the majority - Kaggle pits LLMs against each other as a benchmark to test communication, collaboration, and complex strategic thinking - Provide[ game outcomes](https://www.kaggle.com/benchmarks/kaggle/werewolf/versions/1) as JSON files for public exploration ### Goals - Build an ETL pipeline to parse gameplay JSON files into a full bronze/silver/gold medallion architecture - Create dashboards to explore game progression, compare model performance, identify factors affecting game outcomes, and flag strong/weak model pairs. - Implement unified version control for all resources (pipeline, kickoff job, dashboard) using DABs

## ETL Pipeline and Resource Deployment

 

### Challenges - Environment limited to Serverless compute- costly - Full dataset is 30K JSON game records, each \~7.5 MB; 230 GB total - Variable JSON length => full file ingest before parsing ### Solutions - Work off a game subset (\~1K records) - Limit bronze table to key JSON elements, retain files in Volume - Incremental refresh for bronze table to limit JSON reads ### UC Medallion Architecture - **Landing: ** Volume containing raw game record JSON files - **Bronze:** Single streaming table ingestion of normalized JSON, excluding large unused payloads - **Silver:** Structured episodes, players, actions, and events - **Gold:** Model/team performance summaries and a game timeline ### ETL Orchestration - [Kickoff job](https://dbc-b14fd7ae-c2b5.cloud.databricks.com/jobs/79899079233069?o=7474648320653999) detects file addition to Landing volume, triggers ETL pipeline - [Pipeline ](https://dbc-b14fd7ae-c2b5.cloud.databricks.com/pipelines/fef6524a-702b-4adc-b8e2-9b6a2aa5f70d?o=7474648320653999)loads/parses new JSON files from Landing and incrementally writes to bronze table - Silver and gold data saved as materialized views; incrementally refreshed ### Bundle deployment - `werewolf-etl` DAB wraps all resources under single versioning/deployment framework backed by a [Git repo](https://github.com/jmostowy1/werewolf-etl.git) - Kickoff job - ETL pipeline - Visualization dashboard
